user.title: ISDT charger
user.description: The charger is reached through an isdttool bridge (`isdttool serve`) on the machine it is plugged into.

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the machine running the bridge.
data_description.port: TCP port of the bridge. The first charger on a machine uses 24000, the next 24001, and so on.

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the machine running the bridge.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the bridge, or the charger does not answer. Check that `isdttool serve` runs, and that the host and port are right.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. See the log for details.

abort.already_configured: This charger is already set up. Its address has been updated.
abort.wrong_charger: That address leads to a different charger.

data_description.worn_resistance: A cell whose internal resistance is at least this is reported as worn. Healthy NiMH cells read about 150–300 mΩ.

possible_alkaline.title: Remove the cell from {charger} slot {slot}
possible_alkaline.description:
The charger is charging the cell in slot {slot} as if it were rechargeable, but it behaves like an alkaline. Alkaline cells can leak, or burst, when charged. Take it out now.

This goes away once the slot is empty.

shorted.title: Shorted cell in {charger} slot {slot}
shorted.description:
The cell in slot {slot} stays at 0 V while the charger pre-charges it, so it is shorted inside. It turns the charging current into heat. Take it out, and recycle it.

This goes away once the slot is empty.

long_charge.title: Unusually long charge in {charger} slot {slot}
long_charge.description:
The cell in slot {slot} has been charging for more than 4 hours. A normal AA or AAA charge on the N24 takes less than 2. Check that the cell is a NiMH or NiCd, and that it isn't getting hot.

This goes away once charging stops.
